tei:titleStmt.tei:title: The Four Freedoms, as articulated by President Franklin D. Roosevelt (6 January 1941)

tei:div.tei:head: The Four Freedoms, as articulated by President Franklin D. Roosevelt (6 January 1941)

tei:lg.tei:l: ...In the future days,
which we seek to make secure,
we look forward to a world
founded upon four essential human freedoms.
The first is freedom of speech and expression –
everywhere in the world.
The second is freedom of every person
to worship God in his own way –
everywhere in the world.
The third is freedom from want –
which, translated into world terms,
means economic understandings
which will secure to every nation
a healthy peacetime life for its inhabitants –
everywhere in the world.
The fourth is freedom from fear –
which, translated into world terms,
means a world-wide reduction of armaments
to such a point and in such a thorough fashion
that no nation will be in a position
to commit an act of physical aggression
against any neighbor – anywhere in the world.
That is no vision of a distant millennium.
It is a definite basis for a kind of world
attainable in our own time and generation.
That kind of world is the very antithesis
of the so-called new order of tyranny
which the dictators seek to create
with the crash of a bomb....
